page: Amazon Web Services r7a.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing AMD EPYC 9R14 processors running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the r7a.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The stress-ng multi-core test and Passmark CPU score both rank in the top 10% of tested systems, supported by strong single-core performance in Geekbench and stress-ng. Memory read-only bandwidth reaches 24576.62 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 652.3 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, both placing in the top 10%. Database operations, such as Redis SET, achieve 323.08 million operations per second. However, text generation speeds during LLM inference represent a relative tradeoff, with small model text generation scoring in the bottom 25%.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is defined by its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated compute resources, which reduce virtualization overhead for memory-intensive deployments. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs means resource allocation is optimized purely for memory and CPU-bound execution. This profile is suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and complex memory-bound data processing workloads.
